newsitem.title: INDIA: India scraps minimum equity rule for SIDCs.
newsitem.headline: India scraps minimum equity rule for SIDCs.

text.p: The Indian government said on Monday that it has scrapped a requirement that State Industrial Development Corporations (SIDCs) must hold at least a 26 percent stake in joint venture projects in which they invest.
It said in a statement that "the latest decision is in continuation of the steps taken by the government to provide greater flexibility to investors in important areas of the economy".
Currently, SIDCs and other state government industrial promotional agencies must hold at least 26 percent equity in the paid-up capital of companies in which they invest.

The government said that in cases where the stipulation is currently imposed in letters of intent or industrial licences, entrepreneurs or companies interested in obtaining a waiver of the requirement can apply to the Industry Ministry.
